title: Transmission Range Sensor "B" Circuit (PRNDL Input)
plain: The computer is watching the transmission range sensor "B" circuit and has spotted an electrical fault. This sensor tells the computers which gear position (P, R, N, D) the shifter is in.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Gear indicator may show the wrong gear
May not start in Park or Neutral
Harsh or wrong shifts possible

causes.name: Range sensor out of adjustment or worn
Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the transmission range sensor
Broken or chafed wire in the transmission range sensor "B" circuit
Failed transmission range sensor
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the transmission range sensor "B" circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the transmission range sensor.

title: Transmission Range Sensor "B" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the transmission range sensor "B" circuit and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. This sensor tells the computers which gear position (P, R, N, D) the shifter is in.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Gear indicator may show the wrong gear
May not start in Park or Neutral
Harsh or wrong shifts possible

causes.name: Range sensor out of adjustment or worn
Failing or sticking transmission range sensor
Shift cable out of adjustment
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the transmission range sensor "B" circuit reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the transmission range sensor itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

title: Transmission Range Sensor "B" Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the transmission range sensor "B" circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. This sensor tells the computers which gear position (P, R, N, D) the shifter is in.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Gear indicator may show the wrong gear
May not start in Park or Neutral
Harsh or wrong shifts possible

causes.name: Range sensor out of adjustment or worn
Signal wire in the transmission range sensor "B" circuit shorted to ground or open
Failed transmission range sensor
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring in the transmission range sensor "B" circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Unplug the transmission range sensor and see if the reading changes
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the transmission range sensor.

title: Transmission Range Sensor "B" Circuit High
plain: The computer is watching the transmission range sensor "B" circuit and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. This sensor tells the computers which gear position (P, R, N, D) the shifter is in.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Gear indicator may show the wrong gear
May not start in Park or Neutral
Harsh or wrong shifts possible

causes.name: Range sensor out of adjustment or worn
Signal wire shorted to voltage or a broken ground wire
Failed transmission range sensor
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the transmission range sensor "B" circuit
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Repair the open ground or shorted wire; if the wiring is fine, replace the transmission range sensor.

title: Transmission Range Sensor "B" Circuit Intermittent
plain: The computer is watching the transmission range sensor "B" circuit and is seeing a signal that cuts in and out. This sensor tells the computers which gear position (P, R, N, D) the shifter is in.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Gear indicator may show the wrong gear
May not start in Park or Neutral
Harsh or wrong shifts possible

causes.name: Range sensor out of adjustment or worn
Loose connector or chafed wire that loses contact over bumps
Transmission range sensor failing on and off
Corrosion inside the connector
Poor ground connection

checks: Wiggle the wiring for the transmission range sensor "B" circuit with the engine running while watching live data
Check connector pins for corrosion or spread terminals
Note when it happens (hot, cold, bumps) to narrow it down
fix: Repair the loose or corroded connection; replace the transmission range sensor if the wiring is solid.

title: Transmission Range Sensor "A"/"B" Correlation
plain: The two signals from the gear position sensor do not agree about which gear position is selected.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Gear indicator may show the wrong gear
May not start in Park or Neutral
Harsh or wrong shifts possible

causes.name: Worn or failing transmission range sensor
Shift cable out of adjustment
Wiring or connector fault
Transmission computer fault

checks: Check that the shifter and gear indicator match
Check range sensor readings in each position
fix: Adjust or replace the range sensor, or adjust the shift cable.

title: Transmission Range Sensor Alignment
plain: The gear position sensor is not lined up correctly with the shifter.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Gear indicator may show the wrong gear
May not start in Park or Neutral
Harsh or wrong shifts possible

causes.name: Range sensor not adjusted after transmission work
Shift cable stretched or out of adjustment
Worn range sensor

checks: Check whether transmission work was done recently
Check shifter alignment in each position
fix: Adjust the range sensor and shift cable; replace the sensor if worn.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid "G"
plain: The computer is watching the pressure control solenoid "G" and has spotted an electrical fault. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission sets the fluid pressure that applies the clutches during shifts.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the pressure control solenoid "G"
Broken or chafed wire in the pressure control solenoid "G" circuit
Failed pressure control solenoid "G"
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the pressure control solenoid "G", checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the pressure control solenoid "G".

title: Pressure Control Solenoid "G" Performance/Stuck Off
plain: The pressure control solenoid "G" is not responding the way the computer expects. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission sets the fluid pressure that applies the clutches during shifts.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Sticking pressure control solenoid "G"
Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Worn valve body or internal fluid leak
Worn clutches inside the transmission

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Look for other transmission codes
Have the solenoid tested and commanded with a scan tool
fix: Service the fluid if it is low or dirty; if the code returns, replace pressure control solenoid "G" or the valve body it sits in.

title: Transmission Range Sensor "A" Circuit Not Learned
plain: The computer has not learned the positions of gear position sensor "A", usually after a part was replaced.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Gear indicator may show the wrong gear
May not start in Park or Neutral
Harsh or wrong shifts possible

causes.name: Relearn not done after replacing the sensor, transmission or computer
Relearn procedure interrupted
Faulty range sensor

checks: Ask whether parts were recently replaced
Run the range sensor learn procedure with a scan tool
fix: Perform the range sensor learn procedure.
